quote.text: Before the Law stands a doorkeeper.
quote.author: Franz Kafka, Before the Law, 1915 — the first sentence, for an issue about who gets checked, and when

stories.headline: Turn it over and read the stamp on the tube
stories.dek: The fastest quality test in this category takes four seconds and costs nothing. Everything after it — the badge, the aluminium finish, the leather — is a question about warranties and factories.

stories.kicker: Silicon & Sovereignty · the week the file opened
stories.headline: Eighty thousand payloads, nine hundred links, and a prime minister
stories.dek: Four things landed in four days: independent forensics, a government investigation, an evidence dataset, and a second training halt. The July incident stopped being an incident.

stories.headline: The republic that asked to be refused
stories.dek: Four hundred and sixty-three thousand Kazakhstanis have applied to have themselves banned from gambling. Nine were on the psychiatric register. The gap between those two numbers is a theory of the state.

stories.headline: He told them the day before which evening he would go, and at what hour
stories.dek: Aleksandar Vučić resigned the Serbian presidency on Sunday at eight, eight months early, to run for prime minister on 25 October. Whether that is a manoeuvre from strength depends entirely on a poll nobody can agree about.

stories.headline: Two years before the announcement, and one kilometre from the station
stories.dek: The Government is now pulling individual property records for officers who worked on rail planning between 2007 and 2011. Ten days ago it was reviewing a paper’s methodology.

stories.kicker: Gear We’re Watching · on sale tomorrow
stories.headline: Nine drivers, one HDMI socket, and a ceiling you may not have
stories.dek: The Sonos Beam Ultra reaches Singapore shelves on Tuesday at S$1,299. Two reviewers gave it nine out of ten and one told readers not to buy it — all in the same four days.

stories.headline: Three point four million dollars, and a battery
stories.dek: The most expensive Cartier ever sold at auction is a quartz watch made in 2010. The estimate its own house printed — one million to five — is the part a collector should read twice.

stories.headline: Three wide openings, and a seven-year-old re-release beat all of them
stories.dek: Brad Pitt and a German shepherd took twenty million dollars and an A− from audiences. The sharpest review of the weekend calls the film propaganda.

stories.headline: The phone arrives at twelve. The eating shows up at fourteen
stories.dek: Nearly nine thousand children, measured at the age our reader’s daughter is now and again two years later. The effect sizes are real, modest, and one confidence interval barely clears one.

stories.kicker: The Big Picture · week of 22–26 September
stories.headline: Oil is the engine, the long end is the transmission, and the dollar is the exhaust
stories.dek: The ten-year added twenty-one basis points in a week and the thirty-year reached a level last seen two decades ago. A four-billion-dollar buyback did not slow it.

stories.kicker: Down the Rabbit Hole · the invitation
stories.headline: Nine hundred and eighteen thousandths of an inch
stories.dek: Everything in a letterpress shop is shimmed to one number. The whole craft, and its only real argument, is about how hard you push.

stories.headline: Two hundred and thirty-nine trials produced a number you could put on a fridge. Its authors say not to
stories.dek: Four sessions a week, twenty-five minutes, for thirteen weeks. Then read the sentence where the researchers withdraw it.

stories.headline: One basho sold out in nine days, and one Tokyo show gives you a third of itself per visit
stories.dek: Every row was re-checked this weekend against a venue or official ticketing page.
